# /crav1-tighten-plan

lane: plan | group: Plan | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.0.0 | prompts: 1
purpose: Walk plan.md/tasks.md issues one by one (including /crav1-review-plan P#s).
use_when: Plan findings, or mushy tasks
reads: Reads `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `spec.md`, `claims.md` when it exists, and plan-review findings already in the chat.
writes: Writes only the picked plan issue in `plan.md` or `tasks.md`.
leaves alone: Leaves `spec.md` and application code alone. Leaves a claimed `In progress:` task line in `tasks.md` unchanged.
limits: a spec-tagged finding is not patched here.
flow:
- `reviewed --items <file>` writes the open count the script computes.
- A hand-counted `--open` is not the path.
- with no plan issue left, Run next names `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build <slug>`, never `/crav1-build-tasks`; uncommitted files come first inside Run next as `Commit the <n> changed spec files:` above `/crav1-finalize-commit`.
- the empty queue ends with a Run next entry, its label above the command, no `Next:` line.
- A spec finding already patched, dropped or kept no longer sends you back to `/crav1-tighten-spec`.
- the index (remaining `P#` titles, the current one marked, plan or spec), the finding counts, the dependency waves and ordering problems, the batch card with its findings table, the one empty-queue `Next` line and the `Reviewed:` line come from `scripts/plan_check.py` (`order`, `queue`, `batch`, `reviewed`), a thin copy of the script that ships with `/crav1-plan-from-spec`.
- The typical plan shapes, the empty-queue rules, the Reviewed line, the items file and the suggest step moved word for word to `references/issues.md`.
- the batch is one card.
- `yes (Recommended)` applies every recommendation.
- Typed changes go on that card's free-text answer, for example `P1 A, P3 keep`.
- the batch card is asked only after a findings table in that same reply (Id, Issue, Options, Recommendation).
- The card names each item, for example `P4 tasks miss the 400 path: add a test`.
- It does not say `table above`.
- The command is `<interpreter> -X utf8 <skill crav1-tighten-plan>/scripts/batch_offer.py --title "Tighten-plan batch" --items <file>`.
- It prints no card without rows.
- a task listed in `claims.md` as `In progress:` is left unchanged: no renumber, reorder, rewrite, or removal.
- After writing `tasks.md`, the step preserves those lines and says once which claimed tasks were kept.
- `plan_check.py order` also lists branches that wait for each other as a `Branch loop:` line with the fixes the ready check offers, in the same plain words.
- Each is a candidate `P#` with the new `fix-loop` option.
- The batch yes applies it with `walk_progress.py fix-loop --root <spec-folder> --pick <n> --yes`, which writes the `(map:)` marks or drops the one wait in `tasks.md` and rebuilds `build-map.md`.
- a task line that says `after PR 87 merges` and has no `(after: PR 87)` is a candidate `P#`.
- On yes, `plan_check.py after-pr --root <spec-folder> --yes` writes the mark.
called_by: Called by the user.
runs by itself: Calls no skill.
you run next: /crav1-ado-sync; /crav1-tasks-ready-to-build; /crav1-build-walk; /crav1-build-tasks; /crav1-build-features
first: `/crav1-tighten-plan @docs/specs/<slug>/`
walkthrough: from-spec-to-plan.md
human: https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit/blob/v1.203.0/docs/reference/skills/crav1-tighten-plan.md
